ig_caption:
Bidirectional A* on Real Maps: The Ultimate Pathfinding Algorithm ⚡ How autonomous vehicles and routing AI calculate optimal routes in milliseconds?

Here’s what you’re seeing on a real Amsterdam map: 
1) Two A* searches run at once—one forward from your start, one backward from your destination. 
2) Each frontier uses the same core scoring idea: f(n)=g(n)+h(n), but you keep them separate so work gets split. 
3) When the forward and backward waves meet, you reconstruct the best path with far fewer node expansions than classic A*. 

Tech breakdown (why it’s fast):
- Bidirectional search reduces the effective search depth. 
- With consistent heuristics, both directions stay “goal-directed,” keeping exploration tight. 
- Done right, you get near-optimal routes with a big speedup on large graphs.

Takeaway: If you want faster optimal routing, split the search—don’t brute-force one direction.

Debate question: In real GPS graphs, which would you trust more for speed—single-direction A* with a strong heuristic, or Bidirectional A* with potentially looser reverse assumptions?
